findings.title: SQL injection: user input concatenated into an executed query
findings.summary: user_id is concatenated into the SQL string and executed without parameterisation.
findings.impact: An attacker controls query structure and can read or destroy any table the connection can reach.
findings.explanation: `"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + user_id` puts caller-controlled text into the statement text. Nothing between the function entry and `conn.execute` constrains it.
findings.attack_input: load_user(conn, '0 UNION SELECT name, sql, 1 FROM sqlite_master')
findings.attack_execution: The concatenated string is handed straight to conn.execute.
findings.attack_result: The injected predicate executes and returns schema data the caller was never meant to see.
findings.evidence:
8: 
9: def load_user(conn, user_id):
10:     query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + user_id
11:     return conn.execute(query).fetchone()
12: 
13:

fix_suggestions.label: Use a bound parameter
fix_suggestions.description: return conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone()

findings.recommendation: return conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone()

findings.debate_note: Trigger and wrong result are grounded in the supplied line.
findings.title: Command injection: unquoted argument interpolated into a shell command
findings.summary: `name` is interpolated into a shell string passed to os.system.
findings.impact: A caller who controls `name` runs arbitrary shell commands as the service user.
findings.explanation: `os.system` invokes /bin/sh -c. With `"sh report.sh " + name`, a name containing `; rm -rf /data ;` closes the first command and starts a second one.
findings.attack_execution: The shell parses the metacharacters and runs the appended command.
findings.attack_result: Arbitrary command execution on the host running the report job.

fix_suggestions.label: Use subprocess with an argument list
fix_suggestions.description: subprocess.run(["sh", "report.sh", name], check=True) — no shell is spawned, so metacharacters are inert.

findings.recommendation: subprocess.run(["sh", "report.sh", name], check=True) — no shell is spawned, so metacharacters are inert.

findings.title: Mutable default argument is shared across calls
findings.summary: `values=[]` is evaluated once at import and mutated in the body, so state leaks between calls.
findings.impact: The second call to average() sees the first call's values, producing wrong totals that are hard to reproduce.
findings.explanation: Python binds the default list object at function definition time. `values.append(0)` mutates that same object, so it persists for the life of the module.
findings.attack_execution: The second call starts from [0, 1, 2, 3, 0] instead of [10, 0].
audit_log: No defensive copy exists before the append

fix_suggestions.label: Default to None and copy inside
fix_suggestions.description: def average(values=None): values = list(values) if values is not None else []

findings.recommendation: def average(values=None): values = list(values) if values is not None else []

findings.debate_note: Trigger and wrong result are grounded in the supplied line.
findings.title: Off-by-one: loop runs one index past the end of the list
findings.summary: `range(len(values) + 1)` indexes values[len(values)], which does not exist.
findings.impact: Every call raises IndexError, so average() never returns.
findings.explanation: The final iteration reads index 23+1 = the element one past the last one. Python raises IndexError instead of wrapping.
findings.attack_execution: Iteration reaches i = len(values) and evaluates values[len(values)].
findings.attack_result: IndexError: list index out of range on line 23.

findings.title: File handle is opened and never closed
findings.summary: `open(path)` result is returned from without closing, leaking the descriptor until GC.
findings.impact: Under load the process exhausts its file descriptor limit and starts failing unrelated opens.
findings.explanation: There is no context manager and no finally block, so the descriptor stays open until the object is collected.
findings.attack_input: read_config called in a loop over many files

28:     return handle.read()

audit_log: No `with` block or close() on this path

fix_suggestions.label: Use a context manager
fix_suggestions.description: with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as handle: return handle.read()

findings.recommendation: with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as handle: return handle.read()
